result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_pairwise_similarity()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate pairwise similarity between nodes based on neighborhoods. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L8844-L8989){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_pairwise_similarity( nodes=None, method="jaccard", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Computes structural similarity using various metrics that compare the neighborhoods (adjacent nodes) of node pairs. Returns a similarity matrix where higher values indicate more similar neighborhood structures. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : List of node IDs (integers) or labels (strings) to compute similarities for. Can mix IDs and labels in the same list. If `None` or empty, computes for all nodes in the graph. [method]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["jaccard"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Similarity metric to use. Options are: (1) `"jaccard"` for the Jaccard coefficient (intersection over union), (2) `"dice"` for the Dice coefficient (2× intersection over sum of sizes), (3) `"invlogweighted"` as inverse log-weighted (Adamic-Adar index), and (4) `"cosine"` which uses Cosine similarity. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[list[float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Similarity matrix where entry (i,j) is the similarity between nodes[i] and nodes[j]. Diagonal entries are always `1.0`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node ID or label is not found, or if method is invalid. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} **Jaccard Similarity**: - the most common metric - range: [0, 1] - sim(u,v) = |N(u) ∩ N(v)| / |N(u) ∪ N(v)| **Dice Similarity**: - gives more weight to common neighbors than Jaccard - range: [0, 1] - sim(u,v) = 2|N(u) ∩ N(v)| / (|N(u)| + |N(v)|) **Inverse Log-Weighted (Adamic-Adar)**: - weights common neighbors by inverse log of their degree - rare neighbors contribute more - sim(u,v) = Σ_{w ∈ N(u) ∩ N(v)} 1/log(|N(w)|) - popular for link prediction **Cosine Similarity**: - normalized dot product - range: [0, 1] - sim(u,v) = |N(u) ∩ N(v)| / √(|N(u)| × |N(v)|) **Use Cases**: - link prediction: which edges are likely to form? - recommendations: find similar users/items - community detection: group similar nodes - network embedding: similarity-based features ## Examples {.doc-examples} **Comparing Similarity Metrics** "A" and "B" here connect to exactly the same two nodes, so every metric agrees they're maximally similar, even though the metrics are computed differently: ::: {#ef9bbe76 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=False) for name in ["A", "B", "X", "Y"]: g.add_node(label=name) g.add_edge(source="A", target="X") g.add_edge(source="A", target="Y") g.add_edge(source="B", target="X") g.add_edge(source="B", target="Y") [ g.get_pairwise_similarity(["A", "B"], method=m)[0][1] for m in ["jaccard", "dice", "cosine"] ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [1.0, 1.0, 1.0] ``` ::: ::: IDs and labels can be mixed freely in the `nodes=` list: ::: {#0ce26f54 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} g.get_pairwise_similarity([1, "B"], method="jaccard") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [[1.0, 1.0], [1.0, 1.0]] ``` ::: ::: **Link Prediction with Inverse Log-Weighted** P1 and P2 are only connected through a high-degree hub, so `invlogweighted` (Adamic-Adar) rates them as less similar than Jaccard would, since it discounts neighbors that are shared with many other nodes: ::: {#2c50ee52 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph(directed=False) for name in ["P1", "P2", "Hub", "P3", "P4"]: g.add_node(label=name) g.add_edge(source="P1", target="Hub") g.add_edge(source="P2", target="Hub") g.add_edge(source="Hub", target="P3") g.add_edge(source="Hub", target="P4") g.get_pairwise_similarity(["P1", "P2"], method="invlogweighted")[0][1] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 0.7213475204444817 ``` ::: ::: Jaccard treats the same pair as fully similar, since it doesn't account for how widely shared the common neighbor is: ::: {#d7dc576e .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} g.get_pairwise_similarity(["P1", "P2"], method="jaccard")[0][1] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 1.0 ``` ::: ::: **Similarity Within a Dense Community** Omitting `nodes=` computes the full pairwise matrix. In a small clique, every node shares most of its neighbors with every other node, so similarity is high throughout: ::: {#63dada44 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph(directed=False) for i in range(5): g.add_node(label=f"C1_{i}") for i in range(5): for j in range(i + 1, 5): g.add_edge(source=f"C1_{i}", target=f"C1_{j}") g.get_pairwise_similarity(method="jaccard") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` [[1.0, 0.6, 0.6, 0.6, 0.6], [0.6, 1.0, 0.6, 0.6, 0.6], [0.6, 0.6, 1.0, 0.6, 0.6], [0.6, 0.6, 0.6, 1.0, 0.6], [0.6, 0.6, 0.6, 0.6, 1.0]] ``` ::: :::
